messages:
Lena: Quick UX catch from a customer demo: users missed the required asterisk when we animate labels. wondering if animation + subtle asterisk hurts scanability for keyboard users. cc @Marco @Ravi
Marco: Interesting. Animations can shift layout and move focus outlines — bad for keyboard users. If labels animate, we should ensure the focus ring is persistent and that requiredness is programmatically clear (aria-required).
Ravi: Also consider colorblind/low-vision users: a red asterisk alone is problematic. We should never rely on color; add shape or text. Maybe a small chevron with sr-only text: `(required)` announced to screen readers.
Tess: For long forms, we discovered keyboard users couldn't find error fields quickly after submit because we scrolled but didn't focus. Recommendation: when form validation fails, focus the error summary and provide anchor links that move focus to the first invalid input. snippet: `document.getElementById('error-summary').focus(); invalidInputs[0].focus();`
Omar: Micro-interaction nit: when showing inline errors, avoid animated entrance that pushes content down. Use fade-in + transform but reserve layout shifts for page-level changes only. Pushes confuse screen-reader virtual cursor.
Priya: Copy nit: for required markers, prefer single-word visible text 'Required' in extreme flows, but use sr-only `(required)` for screen readers. Also for inline errors, start with the symptom: 'Missing phone number' then short hint: 'Add country code + area'.
Lena: Proposal: update component library with three states: (1) compact list mode: no visible required markers, show top-note if mixed; (2) form mode: visible 'Required' pill for high-impact fields, asterisk for low-importance required fields, all with `aria-required`; (3) animated labels: disable label animation when reduced-motion is on; always keep focus outline.
Marco: Accessibility checklist for the docs please: 1) aria-required on inputs 2) sr-only text explaining marker meaning 3) focus error-summary on submit 4) anchor links to fields 5) respect `prefers-reduced-motion` 6) no color-only indicators 7) test with NVDA/VoiceOver + keyboard.
Ravi: For destructive confirms: avoid typed-confirm for flows where users perform many actions; prefer modal + explicit checkbox + undo toast. If typed-confirm is used, provide an accessible alternative (e.g., voice-of-screen-reader friendly prompt) and avoid forcing typing on mobile.
Tess: Action items: Lena to update component props and add a reduced-motion example; Marco to write the checklist doc; Omar to tweak error animation patterns; Priya to draft microcopy variants. I'll create the ticket and attach a short recording showing the keyboard fail.
Lena: Thanks all 93. I'll post mocks in the ticket and tag reviewers.
